title: A Method to Estimate Cadaveric Femur Cortical Strains During Fracture Testing Using Digital Image Correlation
protocol: Thaw the femora at room temperature for 24 hours.
Remove any wrap applied prior to freezing and wipe the femur with a dry towel.
Pot the greater trochanter into a prefabricated aluminum cup using bone cement.
Spray the bone with white plastic primer to achieve a thin, uniform coating.
Let the paint dry for at least 5 minutes.
Wrap the bone with a wet cloth to avoid tissue dryness.
Add approximately 1 part water to 2 parts acrylic paint for speckling.
Dip a clean toothbrush in black paint and flick it over the white-coated bone surface.
Let the speckled paint dry for 5 minutes.
Mount the prepared speckled femur in the mechanical test machine by inserting the potted distal end into the fixture.
Tighten two screws to secure the specimen.
Adjust the two high intensity discharge light reflectors to achieve optimal illumination on the femur surface while avoiding reflections in the camera image.
Reduce the aperture of the front and back view high speed video camera lenses such that the entire region of interest is in focus.
Readjust the light reflectors to further improve illumination while reducing glare.
Set the image acquisition software to capture at 6000 frames/s at a resolution of 1024 x 512 pixels.
Set the total number of frames to be acquired after the trigger signal is received to 12288.
Arm high speed video software for image acquisition when the trigger signal is received from the test system.
Save the video to disk by specifying a desired path and file name in the image acquisition software and clicking "Save".
Create separate working directories for front and back views of the femur.
Use video analysis software to open the appropriate high speed video recording.
Note the key frame reference numbers at the start of load frame actuator movement.
Note the key frame reference numbers immediately after the fracture event.
Open and run the "mov_frames.m" script in the working directory for the pertinent femur side.
Enter the ending frame number identified with a step size of 25 - 40 in the resulting dialog box.
Click "Extract Frames".
Inspect the working directory to ensure the *.tiff files were extracted correctly.
Use an external finite element meshing program to create the finite element mesh.
Calculate 2D strains from the differential displacement vectors with the finite element method.
Import the initial extracted *.tiff image into the finite element software pre-processor as a template for spline creation.
Find two easy to identify fiduciary points in the image that are at opposite corners of the frame and record their X and Y coordinates.
In an image editing software, open the same image imported into the finite element software preprocessor.
Record X and Y direction values of the pixels associated with points identified in step 5.2.
Use the spline tool to outline a closed section representing the region of interest in the "Sketch" module.
Seed the edges of the closed section with a global mesh size of 1 mm under "Seed Part Instance".
Set the element shape to quadrilateral under "Assign mesh controls".
Mesh the closed section.
Export the mesh to an ASCII file consisting of nodal coordinates and element definitions.
Copy the node block containing node numbers and coordinates into a new text file and save as "nodes.txt".
Repeat for the element block and save the new text file as "elements.txt".
Create a 2-element row vector called ab1 with the values identified in Step 5.2.
Create a 2-element row vector called ab2 with the values identified in Step 5.2.
Create a 2-element row vector called px1 with the values identified in Step 5.3.
Create a 2-element row vector called px2 with the values identified in Step 5.3.
Save the Workspace as "points.mat".
Run the script "convert_imagesize.m" to register points from the finite element mesh with the extracted high speed video image.
Run the script "rrImageTrackGui.m".
Load the first image ("p01.tif").
Enter the number of the last *.tiff file that was extracted as the total number of images to process.
Load the mesh created in Step 5.7 by setting the mesh option to "Read from file" and clicking "Accept".
Specify tracking values based on guidelines for Tracking parameters.
Set a starting Kernel size of 21.
Set a starting Subpixel size of 4.
Use a starting Smoothness factor of 2.
Set maxMove factor to 10.
Set smoothGrid factor to 15.
Select a guide point with significant contrast, avoiding glare or blurriness.
Click "Check guide" to verify the correlation peak is at least twice the amplitude compared to its neighbors.
Click "Accept".
Click "Perform Tracking".
After tracking completes, click "Animate".
When animation finishes, click "Write strains (post processing software)".
Enter *.exe and select writeStrainRR_simple.exe11.
Close the GUI.
Run "analyzeFailurePrecursor.m" from the command line with an input argument of step size (choose 20 - 30).
Identify peaks in the output, which signify bone damage.
Locate the frame corresponding to the largest peak for global bone failure.
Run "makeMovies.m" from the command window with arguments (numVars, endstep, flag).
Set numVars as specified: displacements (1-3), strain components (4-6), principal and von Mises strain (7-8), or strain energy (9).
Define endstep as the last frame to be included in the movie.
Set optional argument flag to 1 for movies of the specific entity defined by numVars, or set it to 0 for all variables.
Create a finer series of images for DIC.
Identify the frame spacing for three different regimes of interest based on strain rate.
Set large frame spacing for the initial slow-strain segment (e.g., 3333 μs at 100 mm/s displacement rate).
Decrease frame spacing for the intermediate rapid-strain segment (e.g., 1667 μs at 100 mm/s displacement rate).
Use smallest frame spacing right before fracture (e.g., 16.7 μs at 100 mm/s displacement rate).
Run the mov_Frames.m code again specifying multiple frame spacing regimes in the dialog box.
Enter the frame numbers and step sizes identified for each regime in the tool's dialog box.
Create a new directory before running the code to avoid overwriting original images.
Repeat sections 6 and 7 and review results for improvement.
Reduce maxMove setting to 6 when repeating Step 6.5, keeping other settings unchanged.
